note: Fees from the Diplomatic and Consular Fees (Amendment) Regulations 2019; later amendments not yet checked. The same schedule prices processing within 5 working days at a Passport Office (EUR 75 more) or the same working day (EUR 150 more), on the counter fees, and within 5 working days online (EUR 40 more), each written as an urgent route; the passport card is EUR 35 (reference 9), taken as applied for online, its validity not in the schedule (a lead); the online fee for a passport and a card together (EUR 100 for an adult's 34 pages against 75 and 35 apart; 130, 45 and 75) is a bundle the form doesn't hold. Validity is prescribed by the Minister under the Passports Act 2008, s. 9, in regulations not yet found. ireland.ie answered this client with 403 on 2026-10-30, and the Oireachtas site with a CAPTCHA (not circumvented). On 2026-11-03 the schedule's PDF answered with 403 and it was read from the Statute Book's HTML edition of the same instrument; that day the Department's Passport fees page on ireland.ie rendered in a browser and gave the same fees (EUR 75 and 20 online, 80 and 30 by post, 95 and 45 at a counter, the card 35 and the bundles 100 and 45), named the adult's a 10-year passport and the child's a 5-year one (a lead for the validity the data leaves open), and named the counter's dearer services a same-day turnaround (EUR 150 more) and a four-day turnaround (EUR 75 more), where the schedule says within 5 working days, which stands. On 2026-11-03 the Department of Foreign Affairs' fees page (ireland.ie) was read for the passports' terms: a standard adult passport is a "Standard 10-year passport" and a standard child's a "Standard 5-year passport for those under 18 years"; until then the file held no term. The page gives no term for the 66-page passports, which hold none.
